answer: Harvest rights, not extra names, gate admission. Each new key locks a 390-token bond to one numbered tree in a fenced orchard already vacant, and files a sealed blot of dye whose grain forms a private nebula no other key may copy. After a random frost hour, two unchosen walkers who start from opposite flanks of a surveyed knoll must recover that same blot and match its grain map before noon. A reused tree, a shared blot, or a copied map fuses the colliding keys and burns the bond. A farm must fund a distinct tree and an unmatched dye for every alias, so extra names cost more than they return.
